objective.text: Distinguish the initial HTML page response from an Inertia navigation's JSON page object.

difficulty.rationale: Distinguish server responses at initial page load and subsequent Inertia navigation.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: The application uses inertiajs/inertia-laravel 3.7.0 with its standard middleware; server-side rendering is disabled.

stem: The same route returns Inertia::render("Users/Index", ["users" => []]). How do an ordinary initial request and a navigation with X-Inertia: true differ?

options.text: The initial request gets JSON, while later navigation requires a full HTML document.
options.rationale: This reverses the normal initial-load and Inertia-navigation response paths.
options.misconception: This reverses the normal initial-load and Inertia-navigation response paths.

options.text: The initial request gets an HTML document; the Inertia navigation gets a JSON page object.
options.rationale: The adapter selects the root HTML view for a normal request and a page-protocol JSON response for an Inertia request.

options.text: Both receive an ordinary REST array with no component identifier.
options.rationale: An Inertia page response includes component and protocol metadata, not merely arbitrary REST data.
options.misconception: An Inertia page response includes component and protocol metadata, not merely arbitrary REST data.

options.text: Both receive only the rendered component’s HTML fragment.
options.rationale: The Laravel adapter does not normally render frontend component fragments for each navigation.
options.misconception: The Laravel adapter does not normally render frontend component fragments for each navigation.
